chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Durust, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
We mentioned the heads of the sheep, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The head is the place of slaughter, and it is nearest to the pasture and furthest from harm.'
ai.seo_question: Where is the best place to slaughter a sheep according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the head as a permissible site for slaughter (dhabh), emphasizing its proximity to the grazing area (mar'a) and its protection from external harm (adha). This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of minimizing animal suffering and ensuring the meat remains pure by selecting a location less exposed to dirt and injury, thereby upholding the spirit of *ihsan* in ritual slaughter.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Rayyan Bin Al Salt, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Wasity, from Wasil Bin Suleyman, from Dorost, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘We mentioned the head from the sheep, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The head are a place of slaughter, and the nearest from the pasture and remote from the harm’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Ali ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Wasitiy from Wasil ibn Sulayman from Durust who has said the following: “

We once mentioned heads of sheep before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he (the Imam) said, ‘The head is the place of slaughtering (intelligence), close to means for grazing and far from harms.’”
